events.extended_summary: In February 2025, US President Donald Trump marked his return to office by kick-starting a trade war with China. New tariffs, amid accusations that China was failing to prevent the flow of drugs into the United States, set the stage for an escalating economic confrontation between the world’s two largest economies, which stands to reshape global trade. While Trump’s new trade tariffs regime hit allies and rivals alike, China took the fight head-on. Washington first put a 10 percent duty on Chinese goods, citing fentanyl and immigration concerns, and Beijing responded by curbing exports of five rare earth metals key to defence, clean energy and tech products. Then it came to a showdown with Trump’s “Liberation Day” tariffs in April, including 34 percent for Chinese products. events.extended_summary: Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis are trading increasingly intense strikes on strategic sites, including oil infrastructure and ports, marking a sharp escalation in fighting between the two sides. A projectile struck an oil refinery in Saudi Arabia’s southwestern Jazan region on Thursday, killing a Nepalese worker and injuring several others, according to the Saudi Ministry of Energy. The strike sparked a fire and temporarily suspended some operations at the facility, the ministry said. The attack came a day after the Houthis claimed to have struck Saudi Arabia’s biggest oil refinery at Ras Tanura. Satellite imagery taken Wednesday showed a huge plume of black smoke rising from the coastal peninsula following the attack. The Houthi-controlled armed forces said the attack caused a fire at Ras Tanura, part of one of the world’s largest crude oil export terminals, in Saudi Arabia’s Eastern Province. events.micro_summary: Inside Saudi Arabia, Houthi attacks test kingdom's image of security.

events.extended_summary: Yesterday, a group of Russian senators introduced a bill in the State Duma that calls for prison terms of up to five years for illegally distributing information about the aftermath of Ukrainian strikes, as well as terrorist attacks and sabotage. Bans on publishing photos and videos of attack aftermath are already in effect in many regions, though until now the punishment has only involved administrative fines. Now a new article could appear in the Criminal Code as well. Authors of pro-war Z-channels and “military correspondents” reacted to the initiative with unanimous criticism. In their view, almost anything could be classified as illegal distribution, and the bill is aimed at eliminating “unnecessary questions” about how the state allowed this to happen. The Kremlin, however, said that “there is a war going on, and accordingly, the decisions that need to be made during wartime must be made to ensure security.” We present
events.micro_summary: Russia set to criminalise sharing information about Ukrainian strikes.
events.summary: Russia set to criminalise sharing information about Ukrainian strikes.

events.extended_summary: Macy's postponed its Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday at 8:30 a.m. for the first time in the event's 100-year history after a powerful storm brought strong winds and heavy rain to New York City. Organizers delayed the parade Wednesday due to safety concerns about giant balloons, which must stay grounded when winds exceed 23 mph. The storm caused coastal flooding and power outages. Hundreds of performers, including over 500 members of a Texas high school marching band, scrambled for new hotels and meals. The band raised $350,000 in hours from over 2,000 donors. Some performers skipped the event. The parade's only previous cancellations were from 1942 through 1944 during World War II. Forecasters predict dry, brisk weather with temperatures in the 40s for Saturday.
events.micro_summary: The Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade was postponed to Saturday for the first time in its 100-year history due to weather.
events.summary: Macy's postponed its Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday at 8:30 a.m. for the first time in 100 years due to strong winds and heavy rain threatening giant balloons, forcing hundreds of performers to rearrange travel and lodging plans.

events.extended_summary: Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez stated he is confident of securing a left-wing majority in a snap general election scheduled for Sunday, despite public polling indicating an advantage for right-wing parties. Speaking on Friday, the Socialist leader said internal data suggested his Spanish Socialist Workers' Party would win the most votes, enabling re-election with support from smaller leftist allies. Nearly all polls released before a five-day ban on opinion surveys showed a potential coalition between the conservative People's Party and far-right Vox leading. During a televised debate, Sanchez clashed with opposition leaders over immigration, housing, and foreign policy, criticizing the Madrid regional government for honoring Israel during the Gaza assault and calling Israel's actions genocide. He framed the election as a choice between regression and progressivism. The outcome will be watched closely as Europe begins an electoral cycle that could reshape the European Union's balance of power.
events.micro_summary: Spain's Pedro Sanchez confident of left-wing majority in Sunday's snap election despite adverse polling.
events.summary: Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez expressed confidence he will secure a left-wing majority in Sunday's snap general election, despite polls showing a right-wing advantage for the People's Party and Vox coalition, as parties concluded campaigning before the vote.

events.extended_summary: A Russian triple-tap strike hit the center of Kryvyi Rih, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky's hometown, on Friday night, killing a seven-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman and wounding 60 others. Ballistic missiles struck a restaurant parking lot, followed by jet-powered drones targeting rescue workers responding to the initial attack, and a third drone strike hit the location shortly after. Among the wounded were six children, rescuers and police officers, with 28 remaining hospitalized, five in intensive care including a three-year-old girl. The attack caused four fires and damaged approximately 25 apartment buildings, a hospital, schools, an industrial facility, businesses and vehicles. The strike occurred on Children's Day in Ukraine, November 20, in an ordinary civilian area with no military facilities nearby.
events.micro_summary: Russian strike on Kryvyi Rih killed two people and wounded 60 others.
events.summary: A Russian triple-tap strike on Kryvyi Rih, President Zelensky's hometown, killed a 7-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman and wounded 60 others, damaging 25 apartment buildings, a hospital and schools on Children's Day.

events.extended_summary: Round 22 of the 2026 Formula 1 season takes place at the Lusail International Circuit for the Qatar Grand Prix from 27-29 November, despite earlier concerns over the conflict in the Middle East. The 57-lap race begins at 16:00 GMT (7pm local time) with dry, sunny conditions and temperatures reaching 25C. Drivers will be limited to 27 laps on a single set of Pirelli tyres, an increase from last year's 25-lap limit due to reduced downforce levels on the 2026 cars, requiring at least two pit stops during the race. The event follows a chaotic Las Vegas Grand Prix where Max Verstappen won with 352 overtakes, ahead of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri, while Ferrari missed securing second in the constructors' championship after Charles Leclerc made contact with Lewis Hamilton. Haas has also confirmed Oliver Bearman will continue racing for the team in 2027.
events.micro_summary: Qatar Grand Prix set for Lusail with 27-lap tyre limit and 57-lap race starting 16:00 GMT.
events.summary: Round 22 of the 2026 F1 season heads to Lusail for the Qatar Grand Prix from 27-29 November. The 57-lap race starts at 16:00 GMT with drivers limited to 27 laps per tyre set, forcing two pit stops.

events.extended_summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers released quarterback Aaron Rodgers on Wednesday after he publicly criticized head coach Mike McCarthy during a 34-minute appearance on The Pat McAfee Show, and Rodgers went unclaimed on waivers Thursday. The 42-year-old four-time MVP had aired grievances about McCarthy but did not criticize any teammates. Former players Terry Bradshaw and Tom Brady criticized Rodgers for going public with complaints, with Bradshaw calling him a "strange guy" and Brady lecturing him about locker room sanctity. Despite the controversy, some NFL executives left the door open for Rodgers to sign with a playoff contender, noting his arm strength and command remain valuable. Financial considerations complicated potential waiver claims, as Rodgers had $8.56 million remaining on his contract. Rodgers previously led the Green Bay Packers to a 31-25 victory over the Steelers in Super Bowl XLV.
events.micro_summary: Aaron Rodgers was released by the Pittsburgh Steelers after criticizing coach Mike McCarthy and went unclaimed on waivers.
events.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers released quarterback Aaron Rodgers after he criticized head coach Mike McCarthy on a talk show, and he went unclaimed on waivers Thursday, leaving the 42-year-old four-time MVP unsigned despite some interest from playoff contenders.

events.extended_summary: The British Boxing Board of Control has cleared Tyson Fury to fight Anthony Joshua at Principality Stadium in Cardiff, Wales, on December 11 Eastern time (December 12 UK time) after the heavyweight champion passed all pre-fight medical tests. The clearance came after concerns were raised regarding Fury's mental health following statements by his wife, Paris Fury, in a documentary about the boxer. Paris initially used the word "schizophrenic" when discussing Fury's condition, but later clarified that while he showed some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he has never received a diagnosis of the condition. The documentary was edited to remove the reference following her clarification. The Board's general secretary confirmed that Fury cleared medicals and was fit to compete, stating that medical issues would prevent any boxer from fighting regardless of their status. The documentary details Fury's struggles with depression, anxiety and bipolar disorder.
events.micro_summary: British Boxing Board of Control clears Tyson Fury to fight Anthony Joshua on December 11.
events.summary: The British Boxing Board of Control cleared Tyson Fury to fight Anthony Joshua in Cardiff on December 11 after medical tests, following his wife's retraction of claims that he was diagnosed with schizophrenia.

events.extended_summary: Manchester United have triggered their one-year option on captain Bruno Fernandes' contract, extending the 32-year-old's deal through to 2028. The extension prevents overseas clubs from approaching Fernandes when the transfer window opens on January 1. Fernandes, who joined from Sporting for £47m in January 2020, has made 343 appearances and scored 115 goals for United. The Portugal international confirmed that discussions over a new long-term contract have been paused and will resume once United's league position improves. Fernandes is currently a doubt for Saturday's Premier League match against Brentford after returning from the Champions League trip to Sporting with a virus. He scored both goals in the 2-2 draw with his former club but did not train on Friday. Head coach Mauricio Pochettino said he would assess Fernandes' fitness on Saturday morning before deciding whether to risk playing him.
events.micro_summary: Manchester United triggered a one-year contract option on captain Bruno Fernandes, extending his deal through 2028.
events.summary: Manchester United activated a one-year option on captain Bruno Fernandes' contract through 2028, blocking overseas approaches when the transfer window opens January 1. The 32-year-old has made 343 appearances and scored 115 goals since joining for £47m in 2020.

events.extended_summary: The self-styled pastor was arrested in 2023 after the discovery of more than 400 bodies in shallow graves A court in Kenya has convicted the leader of a doomsday Christian cult of the manslaughter of 123 of his followers. Paul Mackenzie was found guilty in Mombasa of ordering his followers, all adults, to fast to death in Shakahola forest near the coast between January 2021 and September 2023. Earlier this month Mackenzie was jailed for 200 years for murdering 191 people, all but one of them children, in the same mass killing. Mackenzie had pleaded not guilty to manslaughter and one of his lawyers said he would appeal against the conviction after sentencing, Reuters news agency reports. Warning: This article contains details which some people might find distressing. The court also convicted 29 others including Mackenzie's wife, Rhoda Mumbua Maweu, of their part in the manslaughter. Sixty defendants were acquitted.
events.micro_summary: Paul Mackenzie: Kenyan doomsday cult leader convicted over further 123 deaths.
events.summary: Paul Mackenzie: Kenyan doomsday cult leader convicted over further 123 deaths. Earlier this month Mackenzie was jailed for 200 years for murdering 191 people, all but one of them children, in the same mass killing.

events.extended_summary: Alleged Russia-directed sabotage across Europe is intensifying, with attacks on rail lines, airports and energy networks roughly doubling over the past year and presenting a risk of mass casualties. Between October 2025 and September 2026, 29 Moscow-linked incidents were recorded in Poland alone, including a November 2025 explosive charge that damaged a rail line linking Warsaw to the Ukraine border, though no casualties occurred. Germany and Poland, which play the largest roles in supporting Ukraine, account for more than half of reported incidents. Meanwhile, new data indicates 720,000 Russian soldiers have been killed since the start of the Ukraine war, averaging one death every four minutes. Such sabotage could bring calls for retaliation and possibly divide European governments.
events.micro_summary: Russia-linked sabotage in Europe roughly doubles with 29 incidents in Poland and 720,000 Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine war.
events.summary: Russia-directed sabotage targeting European infrastructure has roughly doubled, with 29 Moscow-linked incidents in Poland including a damaged rail line, while new data indicates 720,000 Russian soldiers have been killed since the Ukraine war began.

events.extended_summary: Severe storms struck both coasts of the United States during the Thanksgiving holiday, causing widespread disruption. The number of homes without power peaked at close to a million on Thursday evening, with Pennsylvania, Virginia, Maryland and New Jersey badly affected. More than 2,500 flights were delayed and over 450 cancelled on Thursday, with disruptions continuing into Friday. The Macy's Thanksgiving Day parade was postponed to Saturday, marking the first delay in the event's 100-year history. Washington DC experienced its wettest Thanksgiving on record, with nearly 2 inches of rain falling in New York City's Central Park. States of emergency were declared in several states including New York, while bridges closed in Maryland and flooding affected Delaware and New Jersey. The US President said he would consider releasing emergency funds.
events.micro_summary: Severe Thanksgiving storms left nearly a million without power and postponed the Macy's parade for the first time in history.
events.summary: Severe storms hit both US coasts during Thanksgiving, leaving nearly a million without power, delaying over 2,500 flights, and forcing the first postponement of the Macy's parade in its 100-year history.

events.extended_summary: The US Army conducted a controlled detonation of nearly five tonnes of toxic lead azide explosives at an ammunition plant in Iowa on Wednesday morning, with smoke rising shortly after 09:00 local time. The explosives had been stored for approximately 20 years and degraded through recrystallisation, making them volatile. Officials declared the operation a success and issued an all-clear, stating the risk was as close to zero as possible. Environmental Protection Agency Administrator Lee Zeldin reported that air monitors detected zero airborne lead following the blast, while over 1,000 post-detonation samples were collected from homes, parks, farms and drinking water taps, alongside 1,591 pre-detonation samples. Additional sampling at churches, schools and playgrounds was planned for Thursday. President Donald Trump stated that mitigation efforts far exceeded expectations, while Middletown Mayor Rodney Johnson expressed relief. Local soil, air and water testing continues.
events.micro_summary: The US Army detonated nearly five tonnes of toxic explosives in Iowa, with officials reporting zero airborne lead detected.
events.summary: The US Army conducted a controlled detonation of nearly five tonnes of toxic lead azide explosives in Iowa on Wednesday, with officials reporting zero airborne lead detected and over 1,000 post-detonation samples collected from the surrounding area.

events.extended_summary: Ramayana: Rise Of A Legend has become the highest-grossing Indian production of all time in 27 countries, with worldwide collections reaching Rs 1,777 crore in 22 days. The film, directed by Nitesh Tiwari, has set records across North America, Europe, Southeast Asia and parts of Africa, including the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, Thailand, Indonesia, Nepal, Netherlands, Vietnam, Cambodia, South Africa, Kazakhstan, Kenya, Ghana, Ukraine, Finland and Romania. North America emerged as a strong market where the film surpassed Dhurandhar 2. Domestically, the film grossed Rs 1,185 crore while overseas earnings reached Rs 592 crore. Weekly collections included Rs 675 crore in the first week, Rs 357.10 crore in the second and Rs 152.85 crore in the third. Now in its fourth week, the film is preparing for releases in China, Japan, South Korea and Russia in the first quarter of 2027.
events.micro_summary: Ramayana: Rise Of A Legend became the highest-grossing Indian film in 27 countries with Rs 1,777 crore worldwide.
events.summary: Ramayana: Rise Of A Legend became the highest-grossing Indian production in 27 countries, earning Rs 1,777 crore worldwide in 22 days, including Rs 1,185 crore domestically and Rs 592 crore overseas.
